# Additional cut topology and boundary contacts. Answers observed on BigQuery.
# Source: third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/geography_functions.md

# Assert topology and traversal order independently of the last-digit differences below.
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT JSON_VALUE(piece, '$[0][0]') FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(-170 0, 170 0, -170 10)')), '$.coordinates')) AS piece))
=> "[\"180\",\"-170\",\"-180\"]"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(piece)) FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((170 -10, -170 -10, -170 10, 170 10, 170 -10), (-178 -2, -178 2, -174 2, -174 -2, -178 -2))')), '$.coordinates')) AS piece ORDER BY ARRAY_LENGTH(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(piece))))
=> "[1,2]"

SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((170 -20, -170 -20, -170 -10, 175 -10, 175 10, -170 10, -170 20, 170 20, 170 -20))')), '$.coordinates'))
=> "3"

SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 80, 120 80, -120 80, 0 80), (0 85, -120 85, 120 85, 0 85))')), '$.coordinates'))
=> "1"
